articles.title: Bryce James opens Arizona exhibition with a 3 as LeBron begins his 24th NBA season and their family’s next chapter takes shape
articles.standfirst: The father and son are approaching very different basketball milestones as Bryce builds his own path in college and LeBron prepares for another NBA season
articles.summary: The father and son are approaching very different basketball milestones as Bryce builds his own path in college and LeBron prepares for another NBA season
articles.body:
B ryce James made his first shot of Arizona’s exhibition against San Francisco count. The sophomore guard opened the scoring with a three-pointer on Arizona’s first possession, giving him a small but memorable moment as he continues to find his footing in college basketball. Arizona went on to win 93-69 , and Bryce finished with three points, one assist and one steal in 14 minutes.

That first basket arrived just days before his father, LeBron James, is set to begin his 24th NBA season this time with the Philadelphia 76ers . The regular season is scheduled to open Oct. 20.

Bryce is not entering his second year of high school; he is a sophomore at Arizona after redshirting last season. That extra year gave him time to develop before stepping into a college program, and one exhibition game cannot predict how far he will go. But a confident opening shot is the kind of moment that lets him show what he can do on his own court.

Bryce and Bronny are building different paths

The family’s basketball story also includes Bronny James, who is with the Los Angeles Lakers. His move into the NBA brought intense attention, with every performance measured against his famous last name and his father’s legacy.

Bryce is facing a different stage of that scrutiny: he is still developing in college, with more room to grow before professional expectations arrive.

The comparisons between the brothers are inevitable, but their careers will not follow the same timeline. LeBron’s achievements may shape how people talk about his sons, yet neither has to reproduce his career to make his own mark.

For Bryce, the next step is simply to keep learning, earn minutes and turn flashes like this opening three into steady progress.

For LeBron, the new season is another chance to compete at the highest level and make the most of his time in the league by chasing every record within reach, while his sons pursue their own basketball ambitions . For Bryce, this shot is just one step on the path he is forging in basketball, with plenty of anticipation surrounding what he might accomplish if he reaches the NBA.

articles.title: Bill Belichick's controversial dismissal of the college sport that helped UNC forge a 116-year legacy
articles.standfirst: The six-time Super Bowl champion's latest comments have raised eyebrows
articles.summary: The six-time Super Bowl champion's latest comments have raised eyebrows
articles.body:
Bill Belichick has never been known for diplomatic answers, and his remarks about basketball have sparked fresh debate about his relationship with North Carolina's celebrated sporting tradition.

During a weekly press conference, the Tar Heels football coach was asked about basketball and reportedly offered a blunt assessment: “I don't know anything about basketball. Basketball is a pretty simple game. It's putting a ball in a hoop.”

At UNC, the comment carries extra weight. The university has spent generations building a reputation as one of college basketball's most successful institutions, making Belichick's apparent dismissal notable.

The program's history stretches back to 1910, producing generations of outstanding players, iconic coaches and championship-winning teams. The men's basketball team has captured six NCAA national championships, reached a record 21 Final Fours and collected 18 ACC Tournament titles.

Its celebrated legacy includes Michael Jordan and legendary coach Dean Smith , whose influence helped establish North Carolina as a basketball powerhouse.

Belichick's remarks might sound dismissive of a sport that's central to the university's identity. However, his reputation for bluntness suggests he may simply have been expressing his focus rather than trying to insult the Tar Heels' basketball tradition.

Belichick's football rebuild faces its own test

While basketball established UNC's national reputation, football has struggled to achieve comparable championship success. The program has nevertheless produced NFL greats, including Hall of Famers Lawrence Taylor and Julius Peppers , alongside numerous memorable seasons and conference achievements.

Belichick arrived with enormous expectations after winning six Super Bowls as an NFL head coach. His first season in Chapel Hill proved difficult, with North Carolina finishing 4-8 in 2025. The disappointing campaign intensified scrutiny of the coaching change and the university's substantial investment in rebuilding its football program.

There are encouraging signs in 2026, however. North Carolina improved to 3-2 after defeating No. 25 Pittsburgh 21-17 on October 10, securing Belichick's first victory over a ranked opponent with the Tar Heels.

The result offered evidence that his team might be progressing after last season's struggles.

Belichick also praised his current players' commitment while appearing to criticize some who departed the program.

"Generally speaking, this team is more engaged," Belichick told reporters. "They work harder. They're more dedicated and they put more into it, so they get more out of it. And it's important to them. Some of the players that left here, I don't know how important things were to them."

Nevertheless, one victory doesn't erase the challenges ahead, particularly with demanding ACC matchups remaining on the schedule. Belichick will need sustained improvement to convince supporters that his approach can produce lasting results.

UNC's basketball history won't disappear as football pursues greater success. Until football begins competing for major championships consistently, basketball will remain the standard against which UNC's sporting ambitions are measured.

articles.title: College baseball player dies after being struck by a train at age 18: "We are heartbroken"
articles.standfirst: Wheaton College student dies after his car is struck by an eastbound freight train in Illinois
articles.summary: Wheaton College student dies after his car is struck by an eastbound freight train in Illinois
articles.body:
The college baseball community is mourning the tragic death of Tomassino “Tommy” Offer , an 18-year-old Wheaton College student who was killed when a freight train struck his car in Wheaton, Illinois, on Sunday, October 11.

The fatal collision occurred at approximately 10:15 a.m. near Main Street and Front Street, about 25 miles west of Chicago.

According to a Metra spokesperson, Offer had stopped at the railway crossing while a westbound freight train passed. Once it cleared the crossing, he began driving forward, but an eastbound freight train struck his vehicle.

His sudden death has devastated teammates, classmates and friends, prompting heartfelt tributes from those who knew him as a dedicated athlete and a compassionate young man.

Wheaton College baseball coach Matt Husted shared the team’s grief in a statement released through the university.

“Our team is grieving and our hearts are heavy as we grieve alongside Tommy’s family and friends,” Husted said.

He described Offer as sincere, joyful and fiercely competitive, qualities that made him a valued member of the baseball team. The coach also highlighted the teenager’s ability to make others feel appreciated, explaining that he developed meaningful relationships throughout the college community.

Friends and schools unite to honor teen’s memory

According to ABC Eyewitness News, Offer was originally from Michigan and had attended church on the morning of the collision. Reverend Santos Castillo of St. Michael Catholic Church recalled seeing the teenager shortly before he left for Chicago with a friend.

Castillo remembered Offer waving goodbye, reflecting on how an ordinary farewell had become their final encounter.

“I definitely saw him before he left, and he just waved at me, and together with his friend Joe, they were here together, and who would have known that was the last time he’d be in church,” Castillo said.

Students from Wheaton College and the surrounding community gathered on Monday to pay tribute to Offer . The university also held a separate memorial on Sunday evening, allowing students and friends to come together and support one another during an incredibly difficult time.

Notre Dame Preparatory School in Pontiac, Michigan, where Offer previously studied, also released a statement remembering its former student.

“ Tomassino Offer was an outstanding student and an even better young man,” the school said, highlighting the affection he received from teachers and classmates.

Offer had built friendships through both baseball and soccer. His former school also celebrated his sporting achievements, including being part of a soccer team that won a state championship.

His influence extended across classrooms, sports teams, church and college life, leaving behind a wide network of people now struggling to come to terms with his death.

At just 18, Offer had a future filled with possibilities, making the loss particularly painful for his family, friends and teammates.

Authorities are continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding the collision.

articles.title: The shocking confession of Karrueche Tran, Deion Sanders' girlfriend: "I would be embarrassed"
articles.standfirst: Karrueche Tran explains why Deion Sanders’ confidence after losing two toes impresses her
articles.summary: Karrueche Tran explains why Deion Sanders’ confidence after losing two toes impresses her
articles.body:
Karrueche Tran has opened up about her relationship with Deion Sanders , revealing why she admires the Colorado football coach’s confidence following the loss of two toes.

During an appearance on The Pop Exchange Show on October 15, Tran admitted that she might struggle with the same situation, but Sanders hasn’t allowed his medical challenges to change his personality or outlook on life.

“I would be embarrassed or feel not confident with having just three toes,” Tran confessed, acknowledging how difficult it could be for someone to adjust to such a significant physical change.

However, she praised Sanders for speaking openly about his experience instead of hiding it from others.

“He [Deion] didn’t allow this to bring him down or completely change who he is,” said Karrueche .

“I really truly commend him for that and for being vocal about it, too. I can imagine somebody or anybody; I would be embarrassed or feel not confident with having just three toes.”

Her comments followed a photo she shared showing the couple displaying his feet and newly fitted prosthetic toes.

Sanders ’ medical problems began in September 2021, when he underwent surgery for a dislocated toe and an inflamed nerve. Complications involving blood clots and restricted circulation subsequently threatened his leg.

Doctors performed multiple procedures, eventually removing his left big toe and second toe in 2022. Amputation below the knee was also considered.

The ordeal kept Sanders in hospital for approximately a month, even as he remained connected to his coaching responsibilities at Jackson State. Tran recalled the severity of the situation, explaining that his toes had turned black. Their loss also affected his balance, forcing him to adjust how he walked.

Prosthetic toes bring a fresh reason to laugh

Sanders received custom-made prosthetic toes in September 2026, marking another milestone in his recovery. His son, Deion Sanders Jr ., shared footage of the moment on September 16, giving fans a look at the new additions.

The coach welcomed the change with humor, announcing that he was “10 toes down again!” He also described the prosthetics as a blessing and joked that they would help him fill his shoes properly and return to wearing his usual size 11.5 footwear.

Tran has been impressed by how realistic the replacements look, including their carefully designed toenails. However, Sanders still needs time to adjust. His remaining toes have reportedly curved from gripping the ground, while the prosthetics sit straighter, creating a difference he must accommodate when walking.

Humor has become an important part of how the couple handles the experience. Tran affectionately calls his foot “Little Foot” and regularly teases him about it. She explained that being able to laugh together has become a positive part of their relationship.

She also recalled the first time she noticed his foot while visiting his home. Sanders was lying in bed watching television, with his foot propped up and his toes visible. Having never discussed the subject before, Tran didn’t know how to approach it.

“He obviously doesn’t care,” she said of that instance. “He’s not embarrassed.”

articles.title: Tyler Ulrich cause of death: The college player dies at 21 after a serious injury during a game
articles.standfirst: The Southern Nazarene University safety died five days after suffering a traumatic injury on the field
articles.summary: The Southern Nazarene University safety died five days after suffering a traumatic injury on the field
articles.body:
T yler Ulrich , a 21-year-old college football player at Southern Nazarene University (SNU) , has died after suffering a serious injury during a game in Arkansas.

The sophomore safety passed away on Thursday, October 15, five days after the incident that left him hospitalized and prompted an outpouring of support from his family, teammates and wider university community.

Ulrich’s official cause of death has not been disclosed. Southern Nazarene confirmed that he suffered what it described as a “traumatic injury” during its game against Ouachita Baptist University on Saturday, October 10.

Reports identified the injury as a head injury, but the university has not publicly provided further medical details or explained the precise circumstances that led to his death.

The incident occurred during a Division II matchup in Arkadelphia, Arkansas. Play was stopped for nearly an hour as medical personnel treated Ulrich on the field. He was subsequently taken to a hospital, where he remained for five days before his death was announced.

The circumstances have brought renewed attention to the dangers of serious injuries in American football. However, without an official medical explanation, it would be premature to draw conclusions about the specific injury or the events that caused Ulrich’s death.

SNU Athletics shared the news on social media, writing: “It is with heavy hearts that we share the loss of our SNU football player, Tyler Ulrich ,” before expressing its condolences to those affected by the tragedy.

“This loss is deeply felt across our campus. Our hearts are with his family, friends, teammates, and everyone who knew him. We ask that you join us in lifting them up in prayer.”

Tyler Ulrich remembered by his family and football community

The reaction to Ulrich’s death has reflected the impact he made beyond the football field. Southern Nazarene head coach Dustin Hada paid tribute to the player’s character in a social media post, describing the qualities he believed defined him.

“Man of God, ultimate example of quiet strength, loyal, worker, joyous. That’s who Tyler was!!”

Ulrich’s father, Mark, had also been sharing updates as the family waited for news about his son’s condition. In a Facebook post earlier on Thursday, he thanked those who had offered prayers and support while explaining how desperately the family hoped for a recovery.

“Our family is truly blessed to receive all the love and prayers for our young Tyler and we are ever grateful,” he wrote. “But as much support and love that was given, it is with a heavy heart I am writing to say the Lord called Tyler this morning at 11:13 a.m.”

The message marked the end of a painful period of uncertainty for those closest to Ulrich . Although the family had received widespread encouragement, he ultimately did not recover from the injury.

Originally from Azle, Texas, Ulrich was in his third season with Southern Nazarene, a university based in Bethany, Oklahoma. He had started 16 of his 20 appearances for the programme, including six games during the current season, and recorded 36 tackles.

His role as a safety involved helping defend against opposing passing and running plays, making him an important part of the team's defensive unit.

The university also confirmed that its scheduled game against Southwestern Oklahoma State University on Saturday, October 17, would not take place.

Southwestern Oklahoma State announced the cancellation, offering its support to the SNU programme and university community as they mourned Ulrich.

For now, the precise medical cause of Ulrich’s death remains unconfirmed publicly. What is clear is that a young athlete’s life ended following an on-field emergency, leaving his family, friends and teammates to grieve a loss that came only days after the game.

articles.title: Arch Manning continues to fall short of his potential, and the threat of bringing shame on his family looms ever closer
articles.standfirst: The Texas quarterback is facing growing questions about his NFL readiness as his performances fall short of expectations
articles.summary: The Texas quarterback is facing growing questions about his NFL readiness as his performances fall short of expectations
articles.body:
Arch Manning entered the 2026 college football season surrounded by enormous expectations, with many believing the Texas quarterback could emerge as one of the leading prospects in the 2027 NFL Draft.

However, an inconsistent start to the campaign has raised serious questions about his readiness for the professional level, and some analysts are already reconsidering his potential draft position.

Among those expressing concerns is veteran NFL Draft analyst Todd McShay, who recently excluded Manning from his updated top 10 quarterback rankings for 2027.

"Arch Manning — Return. Explore a transfer? — There's still time to turn this season around. I'm more bullish on his NFL future than the social media doom suggests, but another college season currently looks like his best path," McShay wrote on X.

The criticism comes as Manning has struggled to establish consistent performances despite entering the season with considerable hype. Through five games, he has completed 63 percent of his passes for 1,122 yards, recording 10 touchdowns against five interceptions.

Although those numbers aren't disastrous, they hardly reflect the dominance expected from a quarterback supposedly capable of becoming a top NFL draft selection.

His four-touchdown performance against Texas State has also helped boost his overall statistics, making his subsequent struggles more noticeable.

Manning's problems became particularly evident during Texas' 27-24 defeat to Oklahoma in the Red River Rivalry. He threw two costly interceptions, including a pick-six, as the Longhorns suffered a disappointing defeat that intensified scrutiny surrounding their quarterback.

With several regular-season games remaining, Manning still has opportunities to change the narrative. However, he'll need to demonstrate significant improvement if he hopes to restore confidence among scouts and analysts before making a decision about his professional future.

Family legacy increases the pressure on Manning

The pressure surrounding Manning extends beyond his performances on the field. As a member of one of football's most recognizable families, he's constantly compared with relatives who've enjoyed distinguished NFL careers.

His grandfather, Archie Manning, entered the professional ranks after three college seasons, while his uncles Peyton and Eli each spent four years in college before beginning their NFL careers.

Both subsequently became Super Bowl-winning quarterbacks, establishing standards that inevitably complicate expectations surrounding Arch .

Returning for another college season wouldn't necessarily damage Manning's long-term prospects. Additional development could help him refine his decision-making, improve his consistency and demonstrate greater composure under pressure.

Nevertheless, spending five seasons in college might feel like an unwelcome setback for a quarterback who's spent years being viewed as a future NFL star.

Manning's surname can only carry him so far. Professional scouts will judge him on his performances, development and ability to respond when adversity strikes.

A strong finish could quickly restore his draft momentum, while continued inconsistency might make another college season increasingly attractive.

The confirmed national broadcast assignments for this matchup will be ABC and FUBO TV for straming services.

For Texas, the assignment is straightforward but unforgiving: as a three-score favorite at home, anything short of a clean, controlling win will be read as a disappointment. Florida arrives with the freedom that comes with being the underdog. The Gators have nothing to lose and a program-defining upset to chase. Getting double-digit points means Florida's path to a market "win" is wider than its path to an outright one — a backdoor cover, a late score, or simply hanging within a touchdown-and-a-field-goal would vindicate the believers even if the final tally goes against them. For a program hunting momentum, keeping a heavy favorite honest on the road is its own kind of statement.

articles.title: Who is Carter Smith? The BYU student who turned a missed kick into a $3 million College GameDay moment
articles.standfirst: The BYU freshman’s Spider-Man costume and million-dollar field goal made for a Saturday morning he won’t soon forget
articles.summary: The BYU freshman’s Spider-Man costume and million-dollar field goal made for a Saturday morning he won’t soon forget
articles.body:
C arter Smith wasn’t the first raffle winner chosen for Pat McAfee’s “Kicking Is Easy” contest at ESPN’s College GameDay in Provo . The original participant was disqualified after failing to provide identification, and Smith’s ticket was called instead. Then, wearing a Spider-Man suit, the BYU freshman stepped up for a 33-yard field goal in front of a packed crowd.

Smith’s first kick hooked wide right. But the crowd called for another chance, and McAfee gave it to him. On his second attempt, Smith got the ball through the uprights. His fellow BYU fans swarmed him in celebration as the moment turned from a missed kick into a life-changing payday.

The headline-making total was $3 million , but it wasn’t all personal winnings for Smith: $2 million was for him, while another $1 million was pledged to charity. McAfee contributed $1 million, with Ryan Smith and Ryan Sweeney adding the other $2 million between the prize and charitable donation.

Smith is a BYU freshman from Honey Creek, Iowa, and a biology major. He played football and soccer in high school, though the pressure of a live field-goal attempt on national television was a different challenge. Afterward, he told reporters he didn’t know what to expect, said he prayed before the kick and added, “God works in mysterious ways.”

When asked what he’d buy first, Smith offered a decidedly practical answer: “401K!” It was a quick, funny line amid the noise and celebration and a reminder that the freshman was suddenly thinking about what to do with a remarkable windfall.

The moment also set a new high for the contest’s reported prize packages. Earlier this season, Texas student Connor Kacena-Merrell made a second-chance kick worth $1.2 million. Smith’s $3 million package counting the charitable donation surpassed that mark as College GameDay visited BYU before its game against Notre Dame.

articles.title: Colin Simmons, one of the top prospects in the NFL Draft, suffers a concerning injury in Texas vs. Florida
articles.standfirst: The projected 2027 NFL Draft star suffered the injury in the fourth quarter as Florida rallied from behind to stun Texas 27-24 in Austin
articles.summary: The projected 2027 NFL Draft star suffered the injury in the fourth quarter as Florida rallied from behind to stun Texas 27-24 in Austin
articles.body:
Texas suffered another setback as pass rusher Colin Simmons was carted from the field with an apparent leg injury during the Longhorns’ 27-24 defeat to Florida .

The 20-year-old defensive standout went down in the fourth quarter at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium after being brought to the ground while engaged by Florida blockers Lacota Dippre and Bryce Lovett.

Medical staff hurried over before helping Simmons toward the sideline. He was later placed on a cart and taken away for further evaluation.

No immediate diagnosis was announced, leaving Texas supporters anxiously awaiting an update. Before departing, Simmons made the team’s familiar “Hook ’em” hand gesture, though he appeared visibly upset as he headed toward the locker room.

Simmons entered the matchup as one of college football’s most productive defenders and a leading candidate to become a high selection in the 2027 NFL Draft.

He had made eight tackles against Florida and recorded a sack, taking his season total to a nation-leading 10.5. His recent run had been particularly impressive, with 8.5 sacks across his previous three games.

His absence could prove costly for a Texas defense that relies heavily on his ability to pressure opposing quarterbacks. The timing of the injury also heightened the concern, with the contest finely balanced and the Longhorns needing a strong finish to avoid another damaging defeat.

Florida rallies as Texas suffers another collapse

The injury came with the game level at 17-17, after Texas had surrendered an early advantage. The Longhorns led 17-3 in the second quarter, but Florida quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. , making his first career start, gradually settled into the contest.

The Gators found momentum before halftime and tied the score on their opening possession after the break.

Running back Jadan Baugh helped drive Florida’s late surge, as the visitors scored 24 unanswered points and moved ahead by 10 in the fourth quarter. His powerful running gave Jones valuable support and helped Florida take control when Texas struggled to sustain its offensive drives.

Arch Manning briefly revived hopes with a crucial fourth-down completion and a touchdown pass that cut the margin to three. Texas then forced Florida to punt, seemingly setting up another dramatic finish in front of the home crowd.

However, the Longhorns’ comeback stalled when Manning was sacked and fumbled late in the game. Florida recovered, then Jones produced a vital third-down run to keep possession and help secure the upset.

The defeat leaves Texas at 4-2 and adds to the pressure after its previous loss to Oklahoma. The Longhorns had opened the season with national-title ambitions, but consecutive defeats have sharply reduced their room for error in the race for the College Football Playoff.

Simmons ’ status now adds another concern. With no confirmed diagnosis available immediately after the game, the team’s next update will be closely watched by fans and NFL scouts alike.

articles.title: Steve Sarkisian refuses to give Arch Manning a crucial vote of confidence after second straight Texas loss
articles.standfirst: Manning simply hasn’t taken the leap everyone expected him to in 2026.
articles.summary: Manning simply hasn’t taken the leap everyone expected him to in 2026.
articles.body:
It’s safe to say that Arch Manning ’s college football career with the Texas Longhorns has been a rollercoaster to this point. After redshirting as a freshman, Manning had to sit behind Quinn Ewers in 2024, with fans begging for head coach Steve Sarkisian to make Manning the starting quarterback.

That didn’t come to fruition until the following season, but Manning had a very inconsistent 2025 season . His numbers weren’t bad, but both he and the team failed to live up to lofty expectations . So far in 2026, it’s been deja vu for Manning and the Longhorns .

On Saturday, Texas lost its second-consecutive game after starting the season 4-0 and becoming the No. 1 team in the nation. Identical 27-24 losses to unranked Oklahoma and Florida will have Texas on the outside looking in in terms of the College Football Playoff for now.

Steve Sarkisian says everything on the offensive side of the ball, including Arch Manning, will be evaluated after back-to-back losses

The two losses could spark change within the team, and Manning isn’t being assured his starting job for the rest of the season . Sarkisian was asked after the Florida loss if he considered making a quarterback switch during the game.

“ We didn’t play good offensive football. We’re not playing great offensive football right now, so everything is gonna be evaluated. ”

That will seemingly include evaluating Manning’s job security. Manning posted a measly 20.0 QBR (ESPN QB Rating) on Saturday, one week after throwing two interceptions in the loss against Oklahoma - one of which came at a crucial point late in the game that allowed the Sooners to get a last-second field goal.

Manning is simply not getting the job done in an efficient or effective capacity. Behind him on the depth chart is redshirt freshman Karle Lacey Jr. , who has only attempted nine passes through his first two seasons with Texas.

articles.title: Arch Manning and Texas hit a new low with back-to-back losses to unranked opponents
articles.standfirst: After starting 4-0, the Longhorns have suffered two consecutive losses, with Manning playing terribly this week
articles.summary: After starting 4-0, the Longhorns have suffered two consecutive losses, with Manning playing terribly this week
articles.body:
The Texas Longhorns hit an alarming new low on Saturday after suffering a second consecutive agonizing setback, falling 27-24 to unranked Florida at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium .

The shocking defeat closely mirrored their 27-24 loss to Oklahoma in the Red River Rivalry just seven days prior, sending shockwaves across the college football landscape and virtually guaranteeing that Texas will plummet completely out of the top 12 Playoff bracket in the upcoming AP Top 25 poll .

The dramatic collapse is particularly devastating given the sheer difficulty of the remaining schedule for head coach Steve Sarkisian's squad. Over the next month, the Longhorns face a brutal SEC gauntlet featuring back-to-back home clashes against ranked foes in Ole Miss and Mississippi State, followed by daunting road trips to battle Missouri and LSU .

The loss ended a 22-game home winning streak vs. unranked teams for Texas, which became just the third team in AP Poll history , since 1936, to be ranked No. 1 and then lose consecutive games to unranked opponents, according to ESPN Research .

Arch Manning Struggles Under Pressure in Back-to-Back Losses

At the center of Texas' sudden downward spiral are the ongoing struggles of starting quarterback Arch Manning , whose sophomore campaign has taken a major hit over the last fortnight.

After mounting an impressive start to the season highlighted by strong statistical outings in wins against Ohio State and Tennessee , Manning's rhythm has vanished under the weight of relentless defensive pressure and costly mistakes.

Against Oklahoma, Manning tossed two costly interceptions while completing just 19 of 31 passes , and those turnover issues followed him into Saturday's loss to Florida, where a late fourth-quarter fumble inside Texas territory extinguished a 17-3 Longhorns lead and allowed the Gators to complete a stunning comeback.

Through six games this season, Manning's cumulative numbers reflect a signal-caller in the midst of a steep learning curve against SEC competition. While he has accumulated 1,326 passing yards and 11 touchdown passes, his six interceptions and three lost fumbles across six starts have put enormous strain on the Texas defense.

Across these back-to-back defeats, the Longhorns' offense has converted on just 6-of-27 third-down opportunities , underscoring a complete breakdown in execution during high-leverage situations.

With their national title hopes now hanging by a thread and top-ranked SEC opponents looming, Sarkisian and his staff must conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the offense before their upcoming matchup against Ole Miss.

articles.title: Terrifying moment a military officer falls 170 feet from top of Alamodome at UTSA-Navy game
articles.standfirst: The U.S. military officer was set to rappel down as part of the university’s annual “Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans” game.
articles.summary: The U.S. military officer was set to rappel down as part of the university’s annual “Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans” game.
articles.body:
A truly scary scene unfolded before Saturday’s college football game between UT San Antonio and Navy . The matchup was UTSA’s annual Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans game.

For the occasion, four military members were schedule to rappel down from the stadium rafters. But one of the military officers fell from the rafters, falling to the ground at jaw-dropping speed. Once he impacted the ground, medical personnel rushed to his aid.

The ceiling of the Alamodome is reportedly 170 feet high. The officer was transported to a local hospital. As of right now, it’s unclear what the condition of the officer is. Rumors on social media have circulated, but nothing has been confirmed yet.

UTSA posted a statement on the situation midway through the game, with wording that was considered “vague” by many fans.

“ We are deeply saddened by the incident that occurred at the start of tonight’s football game. Our heartfelt thoughts and prayers are with the soldier who was affected, his family and his military colleagues.

We recognize that members of our campus community may be emotionally affected by this incident and are activating wellbeing services to support our faculty, staff and students.”

This is a developing story.

articles.standfirst: Becker regrets making an unsavory comment about the Buckeyes last season.
articles.summary: Becker regrets making an unsavory comment about the Buckeyes last season.

It wasn’t the prettiest game overall, but Ohio State ’s 19-15 victory over Indiana was filled with second half drama. Despite missing two field goals and fumbling the ball away twice, Indiana still had a chance to take the lead late in the game.

Ultimately, Ohio State’s defense came through once more, and secured the win for the Buckeyes. In such a defensive battle, it’s tough to single out one offensive player as the best of the game, but Hoosiers wide receiver Charlie Becker once again showed - in more ways than one - he’s going to be a very high NFL Draft pick next offseason.

Charlie Becker apologizes in person to Ryan Day for "O-H-F-U" comment

After racking up nine catches for 165 yards against Ohio State’s stout defense, Becker showed his impressive character after the game in an on-field meeting with Ohio State head coach Ryan Day . Becker apologized to Day for disrespecting Ohio State after the Big Ten Championship Game last season, which Indiana won 13-10. Becker had six catches for 126 yards in that game.

After that championship game, Becker was caught on camera saying, “ O-H-f**k-you ”. This time around, the wide receiver made sure to let Day know that he was completely in the wrong for acting like that: “That’s not me”.

Becker’s on-field talent has never been in question. His character really hasn’t either, and on Saturday he showed the type of professional he is and will continue to be once he enters the NFL.

articles.title: Arch Manning's last name is dropped after another poor performance: "He's a bad quarterback right now"
articles.standfirst: CBS analyst Damien Harris has delivered a brutal assessment of the Texas quarterback after the Longhorns suffered another damaging defeat
articles.summary: CBS analyst Damien Harris has delivered a brutal assessment of the Texas quarterback after the Longhorns suffered another damaging defeat
articles.body:
A rch Manning 's difficult 2026 season has reached another troubling point, with former NFL running back and CBS analyst Damien Harris deciding that the Texas quarterback no longer deserves to be judged by his famous family name.

Following the Longhorns ' 27-24 defeat to the Florida Gators on Saturday, October 17, Harris announced that he would refer to the quarterback simply as "Arch" until his performances improve.

The criticism came after Texas suffered its second consecutive loss, raising fresh doubts about a team that entered the campaign with national championship ambitions.

Harris argued that Manning's reputation has created expectations that his performances have not justified.

Rather than continuing to discuss the potential associated with the Manning family, the analyst believes the quarterback should be evaluated exclusively on what he produces on the field.

“Until further notice, I’m just gonna call him Arch . Because if you take away the last name, you have a below-average quarterback. That’s what he is, and that’s how we need to evaluate him moving forward. He does not see the football field well. He does not deliver a pretty football. He is not clean in his [operation]… Mechanics don’t look good. Game management doesn’t look good. Nothing about Arch Manning ’s game looks good,” Harris said on the CBS Postgame Show.

He continued his criticism by insisting that the quarterback must demonstrate improvement before earning the respect traditionally associated with his surname.

“ Arch Manning isn’t playing like a Manning . He’s playing like Arch. So until further notice, he’s known as Arch. We need to stop holding on to his last name saying, ‘We’re expecting more. We want to see more. There’s potential out there.’ No. Arch is a bad quarterback right now. And until he becomes a good or a better quarterback, Arch. That’s all you’re going to get out of me. Arch.”

The comments quickly attracted attention among college football fans, many of whom agreed that Manning's background has contributed to the enormous expectations surrounding him.

Texas' latest defeat puts Manning under the spotlight

Texas had an opportunity to halt its slide against Florida, but the Longhorns ultimately suffered a 27-24 home defeat after surrendering an early advantage.

The hosts built a 17-3 lead before Florida fought back, scoring 10 points in the second quarter and adding another touchdown after halftime. The Gators then took control in the fourth quarter, extending their advantage to 27-17 before Texas mounted a late response.

Manning finished with 14 completions on 20 attempts for 173 passing yards and one touchdown.

Those numbers were not disastrous in isolation, but the quarterback's costly final possession became the defining moment of the afternoon. With Texas trailing by three points, Florida forced a fumble that allowed the visitors to secure the victory.

The result followed a 27-24 defeat against Oklahoma the previous week. Manning threw for 260 yards and three touchdowns in that game, but he also recorded two interceptions as Texas fell short.

The consecutive losses have exposed the Longhorns' inability to close out important games and increased the pressure on both Manning and head coach Steve Sarkisian .

Fans question whether Manning receives special treatment

Harris ' remarks reflect a wider debate about whether Manning's famous surname has influenced the way his performances are assessed.

The quarterback is the nephew of former NFL stars Peyton and Eli Manning and the grandson of Archie Manning .

His family history, combined with his highly publicized recruitment, helped make him one of college football's most closely watched prospects before he became Texas' starting quarterback.

Several fans echoed Harris ' argument on social media, suggesting that a less recognizable quarterback might already be facing pressure to surrender the starting job.

“Facts. He would be on the bench if he didn’t have that last name,” one user replied.

“Finally honest evaluation I don’t think ESPN is capable of doing it because they’re scared of the last name,” another wrote.

“This right here! Too much hype but the eye test never lies,” a third declared.

Those reactions underline the growing frustration surrounding a player whose reputation has often been built around what he might eventually become.

However, the debate over his future cannot be settled by his surname alone. Texas must determine whether his struggles are the result of individual mistakes, broader offensive problems or a combination of both.

Sarkisian has indicated that the offense requires a comprehensive review following the Florida loss, leaving questions about personnel, play-calling and execution.

Manning's NFL future becomes harder to predict

The pressure also extends to Manning's professional prospects. Before the season, he was widely discussed as a potential leading candidate for the 2027 NFL Draft, with expectations fueled by his pedigree and perceived upside.

His recent performances have complicated that outlook. Through six games, Manning has thrown for 1,295 yards, 11 touchdowns and five interceptions, according to his season game log.

He has shown flashes of the ability that generated excitement, including a four-touchdown performance against Texas State, but consistency remains a concern.

One possibility is that Manning could benefit from another season in college to refine his mechanics, decision-making and command of the offense. Whether that would mean returning to Texas or pursuing another route would depend on his development and future decisions.

For now, the immediate challenge is to help the Longhorns recover before their next game against Ole Miss on October 24. Another defeat would deepen the team's crisis and intensify questions about the coaching staff's ability to turn the season around.

Manning still has time to improve, but the expectations surrounding him are changing. Harris' decision to drop the family name is a deliberately provocative statement, not a definitive verdict on the quarterback's career.

Nevertheless, it captures the reality facing the Texas star: potential and pedigree can generate attention, but only sustained performances will silence the critics.

articles.title: Duke player faces backlash after athletic trainer is pushed aside during injury scare
articles.standfirst: The incident could bring scrutiny from head coach Manny Diaz and the university
articles.summary: The incident could bring scrutiny from head coach Manny Diaz and the university
articles.body:
D uke cornerback Kimari Robinson is facing intense criticism after an incident involving a female athletic trainer during the Blue Devils’ 24-20 loss to Bill Belichick’s North Carolina Tar Heels on Saturday. The incident, which was captured on television and circulated widely on social media, occurred in the third quarter as medical personnel rushed onto the field to assist an injured Duke player.

Robinson had approached his teammate, DaShawn Stone , who was down on the turf, but the situation took an uncomfortable turn when an athletic trainer tried to move him aside to reach the injured player. Robinson appeared to react by swatting the trainer’s arm away. The staffer briefly looked startled before returning her attention to Stone , who required medical attention and was eventually able to leave the field under his own power.

The exchange became a major talking point, overshadowing parts of a rivalry game that ended with North Carolina earning a 24-20 victory over Duke . The incident could bring scrutiny from head coach Manny Diaz and the university. However, as of the latest reports, no official disciplinary decision had been announced.

Fans demand consequences for Kimari Robinson

The reaction on social media was swift, with many viewers arguing that Robinson should have allowed the medical staff to do its job rather than physically responding when the trainer moved him out of the way. One fan called for the university to investigate the incident and suggested that Robinson should face consequences for his conduct.

The criticism also extended beyond anonymous fans. Former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin II I weighed in on the controversy, posting: “As a man, this just can’t happen. No excuses for it.” The central concern for many viewers was not that Robinson wanted to check on his teammate.

It was that an athletic trainer trying to reach an injured player appeared to encounter resistance from someone who was not providing medical care. Athletic trainers play a critical role during on-field emergencies. They must be able to reach injured players quickly, assess their condition and coordinate care without unnecessary interference. When a potentially serious injury occurs, even a brief delay or distraction can complicate an already stressful situation.

Could Manny Diaz suspend or remove Robinson from the team?

The incident puts Diaz in a difficult position as he manages his team's response to a highly visible controversy. A coach must consider a player's conduct, the circumstances surrounding an incident and the standards expected of everyone representing the program. Diaz and Duke could review the broadcast footage, speak with the athletic trainer and other witnesses, and determine whether disciplinary action is warranted.

Possible responses could range from an internal reprimand or additional conduct training to a suspension, depending on the findings and applicable team policies. More severe punishment would be a decision for the university and coaching staff, not something that can be established by social media reactions alone.

There is also an important distinction between recognizing Robinson's apparent concern for his teammate and excusing his response. Seeing a close friend or teammate injured can be an emotional experience, particularly in the middle of a physical football game. But that concern does not eliminate the need to give medical personnel the space and authority to do their jobs.

Robinson's intentions cannot be determined from a short video alone. The footage does, however, show an exchange that has raised legitimate questions about how players should respond when medical staff need immediate access to an injured teammate. As of the latest available reporting, Duke had not announced a punishment for Robinson.
